# Teacher Feedback Roundtable on DashTeach

Date: 2024-12-10  
Attendees: Saskia Silvhollow, Rhosyn Jorvham, Dorrit Peltdale  

**Agenda:**  
- Review current DashTeach dashboard usability based on teacher feedback  
- Discuss reporting feature enhancements to improve district-level procurement insights  
- Identify priority improvements for Q1 2025 release  

**Discussion:**  
Saskia opened with a summary of survey results from 125 teachers across three pilot districts using DashTeach. Key pain points highlighted were:  
- Over 40% found mastery tracking graphs confusing, especially for multi-subject classes  
- Nearly 30% requested more customizable alert thresholds for student performance dips  
- Requests for exportable summary reports increased by 25% since last quarter  

Rhosyn shared feedback from two district procurement officers:  
- They value dashboard analytics but want clearer visuals that aggregate student mastery at grade and school levels  
- Suggested adding benchmark comparisons against district averages to guide resource allocation  

Dorrit demonstrated a prototype dashboard update incorporating conditional color-coding and simplified navigation tabs. Early reactions from 15 teachers in a closed trial were positive, with 87% saying it improved usability.  

**Decisions:**  
- Prioritize redesign of mastery tracking charts to include multi-subject filters and clearer legends  
- Develop exportable district summary reports with benchmark comparisons by March 2025  
- Implement customizable alert thresholds customizable per teacher by April 2025  

**Action Items:**  
- Saskia to coordinate additional teacher usability tests on prototype by 2025-01-15  
- Rhosyn to draft detailed requirements for district summary reports by 2024-12-20  
- Dorrit to begin development on alert threshold customization feature starting 2025-01-10
